items.title: SPHMC first Picard Gaussian input law

source.anchor: Algorithm 3.1 lines 282–300 and Lemma D.4 lines 2177–2181
source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. Samplinglib supplies omitted measure-theoretic details; this is not the authors' original wording or a complete D.7 claim.

items.statement: Construct the actual independent first refresh noise and finite first-layer Picard Gaussian array, with all measurable and second-moment facts needed by the existing layerwise bound.
assumptions: Incoming phase-state probability law with integrable energy bounded by M≥0.
h≥0, finite Picard index, finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel state space.

obligations.label: Coordinate measurability, integrability and exact moments

bindings.boundary: No repeated phase history, D.3/M_kappa adapter, second array, second refresh, quadrature construction, complete D.7, D.8 or theorem result.

assumption_deltas.source: Algorithm 3.1 says all displayed Gaussian variables are independent.
assumption_deltas.lean: The first refresh and first innovation array are represented by nested product measures.
assumption_deltas.reason: Product measures make the stated freshness semantic rather than an informal label.

assumption_deltas.source: Lemma D.4 uses Gaussian second moments without spelling out measurability or integrability.
assumption_deltas.lean: Every coordinate is proved measurable and square-integrable with exact moment finrank(E).
assumption_deltas.reason: These conditions are required before the expectations in D.7 are legal.

assumption_deltas.source: Algorithm 3.1 samples a second array and zeta_1 later in the phase.
assumption_deltas.lean: This deliberately scoped declaration constructs only the variables consumed by the already-formalized first two query-center layers.
assumption_deltas.reason: It formalizes an exact initial segment of the algorithm; later phase outputs are explicitly separate rather than treated as implicit premises.
